newsitem.title: USA: Florida business activity, profits hold steady.
newsitem.headline: Florida business activity, profits hold steady.

text.p: Florida business chiefs saw little change in activity or profitability over the past year, but their perception of the state's business climate has dimmed, Florida Chamber of Commerce said in a quarterly survey released Thursday.

In the Fall 1996 Issues Survey of the Florida Chamber/Mason-Dixon Business Poll, 41 percent of respondents reported higher business activity than a year ago, 26 percent report lower and 32 percent were unchanged.
Twenty-nine percent said profits were higher than a year ago, another 29 percent said profits were lower, and 42 percent said they were unchanged.

The number of full-time employees was more volatile than in past surveys, with 32 percent of respondents reporting they had more employees than a year ago, 26 percent reporting fewer and 42 percent unchanged.
Fewer respondents perceived Florida as a good place to do business.

In September 1995, 62 percent said Florida's overall business environment was attractive enough to expand operations, 25 percent said it was not, and 13 percent had no answer. In September 1996, 54 percent said it was attractive enough, 43 percent said it was not and only three percent had no answer.
Chamber Executive Vice President Blake Wilson said the change reflected growing concerns about lawsuits and liability insurance.

In September 1995, 20 percent of respondents said they had stopped offering a product or service because of the insurance cost or the fear of a lawsuit, while 78 percent said they had not. In September 1996, 34 percent said yes and 65 percent said no.
The poll was based on telephone surveys with 481 randomly selected Chamber members who were either owners, chief executives or top managers of their firms. The error margin is 4.9 percent.
Jobs and the economy tied with government regulation as the respondents' greatest business concern, while taxes ranked next.

The survey also found increased usage of health-maintenance organziations for employee health insurance programs, and increasing satisfaction with the state's workers' compensation law. But a growing number of members said property insurance was more difficult to obtain than a year ago.
